activity_context.topic_title: Constrained Optimization of Quadratic Forms: Determining Where Extrema are Attained

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{4}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=4$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{4},$ 

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -8 \\ -16 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}32 & -32 \\ -32 & -16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}32-\lambda  & -32 \\ -32 & -16-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (32-\lambda )(-16-\lambda )-1\,024 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-16\lambda -1\,536 & =0 \\ (\lambda -48)(\lambda +32) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =48,\,-32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}=48.
$$
